_about: Curated judgements for the status report (owner: status-reporter). Read by scripts/status_report.py together with docs/features.json and the live board, gates and ledger. Everything here is a judgement that must be traceable to evidence ids listed under 'evidence'; the script refuses to render if the judgements contradict the gate checklists. Written for a technically capable reader who does not know the repo: spell out abbreviations, no file names or task ids in the executive fields.

project.name: HX Stomp Tone Matcher
project.goal: Give the tool a song and get back a preset for the Line 6 HX Stomp guitar pedal that sounds like the guitar on the recording, checked on the real pedal. It works by trying candidate presets, comparing the sound with the recording, and adjusting until they match.

health.rationale: The method that decides whether a preset sounds like the target has not been validated, so the next milestone (recovering presets whose answer is known) has no evidence yet. The first milestone is signed off and there is no hard blocker on the human today, so the project is not Blocked.

technical.rationale: In the last two days both sound engines became fully scriptable, a rendering speed and memory problem was fixed, presets are now verified after every write, and a first real song was matched by hand. Engineering is moving quickly even though the main user-facing question is still open.

breakdown.implemented: Control of both sound engines, preset reading and writing, guitar separation, a reference clean-guitar picker, four tone-comparison measures, an optimiser, a block-by-block rendering method and a block measuring kit.
breakdown.integrated: A hand-run script takes one prepared song section through separation, clean-guitar choice, search and preset export on one machine. Nothing runs from a single command and the pedal check is manual.
breakdown.tested: Automated tests cover all of the above, mostly with fake engines or non-Helix stand-in signals.
breakdown.verified: Engine control and preset checking were verified on real hardware (macOS, pedal firmware 3.50). Matching quality is verified only by one informal listen, not by a blind test.
breakdown.unfinished: Trusting the tone comparison, the known-answer benchmark on Helix, the library of measured blocks, a one-command song-to-preset tool, blind listening and anything beyond macOS.

readiness.rationale: Important pieces have been demonstrated working: a real song was matched by a script, the preset loaded on the pedal and the owner listened to it.
readiness.blocker_to_next: Integrated needs the pieces to run together without hand-holding: one command from song to a pedal-checked preset, using a tone comparison that has been shown to pick correctly. Neither exists yet.

summary: The goal is a tool that listens to a recorded guitar tone and builds a matching preset for the HX Stomp pedal. The building blocks now work: the software can run both of its sound engines by itself, write preset files the pedal accepts, and check what it wrote. One real song has been taken through the whole chain by hand, and the owner found the result promising in an informal listen. What is missing is proof that the tool's own sense of what sounds similar can be trusted. On that song it could not tell its top two candidates apart, while the listener clearly preferred one. Until that judgement is validated, automatic matching cannot be relied on, and no blind listening test has been run. The next step is to test that judgement against presets whose correct answer is known.

biggest_problem.why: Every automatic decision the tool makes (which preset is better, when to stop searching) depends on this comparison.

Gate 1.goal: Prove both sound engines can be driven by code, and that a generated preset loads on the pedal.
criteria_plain: Helix Native renders a test clip from code (smoke test passes).
The HX Stomp renders the same test clip from code on at least one operating system.
A generated preset file is accepted by HX Edit and loads on the pedal.
The shared engine interface is frozen and the control routes are documented.
Gate 1.demonstrated: All four criteria are evidenced and the owner signed off on 2026-10-14. Caveats the owner accepted: the pedal result rests on one operating system and firmware 3.50; the pedal-load result was reported by the owner, not observed by an automated test.
Gate 1.remaining: Nothing for the gate itself. Windows and Linux pedal control remain unverified.
Gate 1.next_action: None. Re-check on firmware 3.80 only if the owner decides to update the pedal.

Gate 2.goal: Show the tool can recover a known answer: given audio made from a preset we already know, its comparison measure picks the true preset and its search finds the right blocks and settings, at thresholds agreed in advance.
criteria_plain: On the known-answer set, the tone-comparison measure ranks the true preset first at the agreed threshold.
Block types, amp and effect models, and parameter values are identified within the agreed accuracy.
A curve showing how accuracy falls as guitar separation gets worse has been recorded.
Gate 2.demonstrated: Working targets were approved by the owner (not frozen). The labelled test items exist but have not been rendered through Helix. On stand-in signals, the best single comparison term put the true preset first in roughly 1 of 8 held-out cases, against a working target of 19 of 20 on the real set; stand-in results are not admission evidence.
Gate 2.remaining: Render the known-answer set through Helix Native, run the real trust check, measure baselines and freeze the thresholds, run the recovery test, and record the separation stress curve.
Gate 2.blocking: The comparison measure has not passed validation on Helix audio, and the known-answer set has not been rendered.
Gate 2.next_action: Render the known-answer set through Native (now possible without a person) and run the trust check on it.

Gate 3.goal: Show that, for real songs, the tool's preset beats the nearest ready-made community preset in blind listening.
criteria_plain: In blind listening on a 20-song set, the matched preset is preferred over the nearest community preset on most songs.
The difference between the pedal and Native on firmware 3.80 has been recorded.
Native-mode and pedal-mode matching have been compared on the same songs.
Gate 3.demonstrated: One song section was matched and listened to informally (not blind). Pedal versus Native agreement was measured on firmware 3.50 for a few presets.
Gate 3.remaining: Gate 2, the 20-song set, a blind listening tool and sessions, and the firmware 3.80 and engine comparison measurements.
Gate 3.blocking: Depends on Gate 2, on song selection, and on a blind listening tool that does not exist yet.
Gate 3.next_action: Wait for Gate 2. The owner can start choosing songs now.

issues.title: The tone comparison is not validated
issues.problem: The tool scores how close two guitar sounds are with several measures, and none has passed the required accuracy test on audio from the real Helix engines.
issues.impact: The optimiser cannot be trusted to pick a genuinely matching preset, so Gate 2 cannot be passed and automatic matching cannot be offered. On the one real song, the top two candidates scored 6.935 and 6.950 (lower is better), a gap too small to mean anything, while the listener clearly preferred one; the best score also swung from 7.7 to 22.7 depending on which clean guitar recording was used.
issues.cause: Measures were built and checked on non-Helix stand-in signals, where the best one chose the right answer first only about 1 time in 8. Real Helix audio has not yet been tried because the known-answer set has not been rendered. The score also ignores loudness.
issues.resolution: Render the known-answer set through Native, run the trust check on each measure, and combine or replace measures until the agreed accuracy is reached.
issues.owner: benchmark and tone-metrics, with the lead freezing the thresholds
issues.next_step: Render the known-answer set through Native and run the trust check on it.

issues.title: The pedal and Native disagree on one cabinet setting
issues.problem: The cabinet's Early Reflections setting does not sound the same on the pedal and in Native.
issues.impact: A preset found on the fast Native engine can sound different on the real pedal. At the value the search chose, the two engines' recordings cancel by only 3.6 dB (poor agreement); with the setting at 0 they cancel by 31 dB (close agreement).
issues.cause: Not yet known. Candidates are an older algorithm in the pedal, a different parameter scale, or a delay-structure difference. Other parameters tested at their extremes agreed.
issues.resolution: Find the cause, or measure every searchable parameter on both engines and let the search free only the parameters that agree.
issues.owner: native-engine and stomp-engine; benchmark for the per-parameter audit
issues.next_step: Run the per-parameter agreement audit; until then any preset meant for the pedal keeps this setting at 0.

issues.title: Guitar separation quality on real songs is unknown
issues.problem: The step that isolates the guitar from a full mix has only been scored on an artificial mix. One real song was processed without a quality score.
issues.impact: If the isolated guitar contains drums, vocals or artifacts, the tone comparison will chase those instead of the guitar and Gate 3 results will be unreliable.
issues.cause: No real-song stress set exists, and the only separation model aimed at guitar has no stated licence so it was not used.
issues.resolution: Run the separation stress test on a few real songs, locally, and record how accuracy falls as the mix gets denser.
issues.owner: separation, after the owner supplies songs
issues.next_step: Owner chooses the first songs (one action covers this and the Gate 3 song set).

issues.title: No blind listening has happened, and the tool for it does not exist
issues.problem: The only listening so far was informal and unblinded. The tool that prepares blind A/B sessions is not built.
issues.impact: Whether matches actually sound better than a ready-made preset is unknown, and Gate 3 cannot start.
issues.cause: Blind sessions need matched presets from the whole pipeline, which does not exist yet.
issues.resolution: Build the session tool once the pipeline produces candidates, then run sessions on the chosen songs.
issues.owner: benchmark builds the tool; the owner listens
issues.next_step: Nothing until Gate 2 produces trustworthy candidates; avoid asking the owner to listen earlier.

issues.title: The library of measured blocks does not exist yet
issues.problem: The per-block approach needs every effect block measured through Native, and the measuring kit has never been run on Helix.
issues.impact: Choosing amp and effect models from measurements (instead of trying them blindly) is not possible, which makes the search space larger than it needs to be.
issues.cause: The measuring kit was only finished offline on stand-in blocks. Native's current host is mono, so stereo blocks and dual cabinets cannot be measured; one unexplained accuracy floor remains when an amp follows other blocks.
issues.resolution: Render the measuring signal through Native for a few blocks first, set tolerances from repeat-render spread, then capture the library overnight for mono blocks.
issues.next_step: Build the Native rendering of the measuring signal.

issues.title: Everything is verified on one computer, one pedal firmware, with a private helper
issues.problem: Pedal control is verified on macOS and firmware 3.50 only, and the small helper program that talks to the pedal is intentionally not published.
issues.impact: Other users on Windows or Linux may not be able to use pedal mode, and others cannot reproduce the pedal measurements.
issues.cause: Only one machine is available, and the helper's source is withheld on the owner's decision.
issues.resolution: Publish a wrapper or rewrite the helper to the documented protocol; test on other systems when machines exist.

issues.title: What the Line 6 licence agreements allow for training is not recorded
issues.problem: The owner read the licence agreements but the findings are not in the repository.
issues.impact: It decides whether models trained on Native renders may be published; it blocks nothing until the learning stage.
issues.cause: Recording the finding was left to the owner.
issues.resolution: Write the relevant clauses' conclusions into the licence notes.
issues.next_step: Covered by the owner action about the licence agreements.

issues.title: A few task-board lines are stale
issues.problem: Several task lines say less or more than the ledger shows (see the technical details for the list).
issues.impact: Anyone reading only the board will misjudge progress; no product impact.
issues.cause: Work moved faster than board edits.
issues.resolution: The lead updates the lines at the next planning step.
issues.next_step: Update the board at the next planning step.

recent_changes.text: Gate 1 was signed off: both engines are driven by code and a generated preset loads on the pedal.
Helix Native now loads new sounds without a person at the keyboard and renders about seven times faster, and it stopped running out of memory.
The pedal write is now checked parameter by parameter. This traced and fixed a bug that made a delay run far too wet when the owner played a preset live on the pedal.
A first real song section was matched end to end and loaded on the pedal. The result was informal progress, not a validation.
Rendering a chain one block at a time matched rendering it whole on a test chain, which opens the way to measuring blocks individually.
A new problem was found: one cabinet setting sounds different on the pedal and in Native. Presets for the pedal keep it at 0 for now.
The first real-song run showed the tone score is not reliable: its top two candidates were almost tied and the listener preferred one clearly.
A silent bug that could reuse an outdated Native setup (and made one measurement look much worse than it was) was found and fixed; the false result was voided.

Two extra tone-comparison measures were added (a sharper loudness-shape measure and a learned audio embedding). Neither came close to the target on stand-in signals, so they did not move Gate 2 forward.
The block measuring kit was finished offline. It has not touched Helix yet, so it does not advance readiness until it is run.
The owner approved the per-block approach (measure and search block by block). It adds work before Gate 2 but shrinks the search space.

glossary.definition: Direct Input: a clean, unprocessed guitar recording, before any amp or effects.
Digital Signal Processing: the audio calculations inside amps and effects.
The software licence agreement shown when installing a product.
An optimisation algorithm used to search for suitable settings.
The Line 6 guitar-effects pedal this project targets.
Line 6's software version of the Helix sounds; it runs as a plugin and renders audio offline.
Line 6's editing program for the pedal; it also imports preset files.
A saved sound: a chain of amp, cabinet and effect blocks with their settings (an .hlx file).
One of up to three stored variations of a preset that the pedal can switch between.
The software running inside the pedal.
The score the optimiser tries to lower: how different two sounds are. Lower is a closer match.
The loss: the combined measures of how similar two guitar sounds are.
Test audio made by ordinary software effects instead of Helix. Useful for early checks; not proof the method works on Helix.
A test set made by rendering presets we already know through Helix, so we can check whether the tool recovers them.
Test items not used when tuning, so the result is not flattered by tuning.
A test of whether a measure puts the true preset first among many candidates.
What is left when one recording is subtracted from another that should match. Reported in decibels below the signal; the more negative, the closer.
Decibel, a logarithmic loudness or level-difference scale.
A cabinet setting that adds the first short echoes of the room.
Splitting a full mix into instruments so the guitar can be analysed alone.
One element in a preset's chain: an amp, cabinet, drive pedal, delay and so on.
The project's append-only record of measured runs; a claim without a row did not happen.
A milestone with a written checklist and a human sign-off.
A listening test where the listener does not know which option is which.
Reading the pedal's settings back after writing them to confirm they match.
A control message that moves one knob or switch from software.
Short for firmware, the pedal's built-in software. The pedal was on version 3.50 until 2026-10-15 and is now on 3.80.
Play a test signal through a preset and record the audio that comes out.
The one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain: the preset file is loaded into its editor and the resulting state is recorded.
Agreement between the two engines: the same preset is rendered on both and the recordings are compared.
Several copies of Helix Native running at once, each rendering a different candidate, to finish a batch sooner.
Extra audio played before the part that is recorded, so delays and reverbs start from the same state every time.
The two signal paths of the HX Stomp. Using both at once renders two chains in one pass.
Real elapsed time on a clock, as opposed to computing time.

engines._about: Wording for the 'Engines: what each can do and how fast' section. The capability verdicts are curated judgements from the ledger, DECISIONS, notes and board (cite them inline; they become links). Numbers written as {t:key:engine} are filled from the ledger every run, so they cannot go stale. 'fw350': true appends 'verified on fw 3.50, recheck on 3.80 pending' until a person re-checks on firmware 3.80 and clears the flag. All timings and the 100-test estimates are computed by scripts/engine_timing.py; nothing about time is written by hand here.
engines.units: Times are in seconds (s), minutes (min) and hours (h). A render is one pass of a test signal through a preset, recorded as audio. A score is one comparison of a rendered candidate against the target tone (lower is better). A capture is the one-off step that teaches Helix Native a new chain, by loading the preset file into its editor and recording its state. A parity check renders one preset on both engines and compares the two recordings. Estimates are 100 times the newest measured time; every estimate says which measurement it uses and its date.

render_2s.label: One render of a 2 s test clip
render_2s.means: Play a 2 second test signal through a preset and record the result.

render_10s.label: One render of a 10 s clip
render_10s.means: The same, with a 10 second excerpt (the size a song-section search uses).

score.label: One comparison (score) of a candidate against a target
score.means: Measure how far a rendered candidate is from the target tone.

parity.label: One parity comparison (per preset)
parity.means: Render one preset on both engines, then analyse how closely the two recordings agree.

smoke.label: One engine smoke test
smoke.means: The quick end-to-end check that an engine loads a preset and returns sound.

search_run.label: A search run, wall-clock per render call
search_run.means: Total run time divided by the renders it made, engine start-up included.

load.label: One preset load or model change
load.means: Stomp: one whole-document write of a generated preset. Native: load a stored template.

capture.label: First-time capture of a new chain
capture.means: Native only: teach the engine a chain it has not seen. Once per chain.

probe_pass.label: One probe pass through an engine
probe_pass.means: Play the block-probe test signals through one block and record them.

probe_analysis.label: One probe analysis (offline)
probe_analysis.means: Check the probe analysis code against known software blocks; no engine involved.

trial.label: One search trial (render + score)
trial.means: One candidate setting: render it, then score it. Scoring time is taken from the score row above.

combined_testing.label: Combined: testing
combined_testing.means: Engine smoke test per engine, and one parity comparison per preset on both.

combined_comparison.label: Combined: comparison
combined_comparison.means: Scoring a candidate against a target.

combined_modelling.label: Combined: modelling
combined_modelling.means: One search trial plus a capture (Native) or a preset write (Stomp).

capabilities.capability: Load a generated preset file (.hlx) directly

stomp.verdict: Yes. The file is compiled and written whole into the pedal's working memory, then read back parameter by parameter before anything is rendered; about 40 whole writes, all read back as written (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). 4 of 4 generated files were written and rendered (ledger 2026-10-14T23:47:43+00:00). Takes {t:load:stomp}.

native.verdict: Yes, with no person, on macOS: a script drops the file into Native's editor and records the state as a template, then renders from the template (ledger 2026-10-14T23:58:32+00:00). A stored template loads in {t:load:native}; a chain never seen before needs a capture first (see below).

capabilities.capability: Export or save a preset file

stomp.verdict: Our own writer produces the .hlx; a human imports it in HX Edit (accepted, ledger 2026-10-14T17:38:00+00:00). The engine never saves to the pedal's flash memory, by policy: it edits the working copy only and puts the original preset back (DECISIONS 2026-10-14 stomp-engine, T003 hardware batch and T004).

native.verdict: Not done and not needed for matching: the generated .hlx is the source, and Native's captured state is kept as a local template, not exported as a file.

stomp.verdict: Yes, at full resolution. Parameters are set in place and checked by read-back to within one hundred-thousandth of the parameter's range (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 stomp-engine, T051 whole-write readback).

native.verdict: Only parameters given a MIDI control number at capture, in 128 steps across each range; everything else stays as captured. Inside that grid it equals a freshly captured file almost exactly (ledger 2026-10-15T20:46:58+00:00). On the 8-block test chain 54 of 63 mapped parameters moved the sound (ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00).

capabilities.capability: Change models (swap an amp, cab or effect)

stomp.verdict: Yes. Any model or layout change is one whole write with read-back, never the pedal's own model command (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes). {t:load:stomp} per write.

native.verdict: Not live. A new model or layout needs a new capture ({t:capture:native}, once per chain); only chains already captured can be rendered. The per-block library that would remove this is not captured yet (T048).

capabilities.capability: Switch blocks on and off by script

stomp.verdict: Yes. Bypass is toggled in place with a MIDI control (the delay's bypass moved with CC 110, ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00), and is part of every whole write.

native.verdict: Yes. Each block's bypass is a MIDI control number in the captured template; one capture reproduces every bypass pattern almost exactly (-328.7 dB against files captured one by one, ledger 2026-10-15T21:31:30+00:00). Only chains captured since 2026-10-15 have it; older templates keep fixed bypass states (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass).

stomp.verdict: Path A and Path B give twice the renders per pass (ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00), but each two-path render differs from a single-path render by -18 to -22 dB (cause unknown), so use it only to compare two-path renders with two-path renders. The pause on writing two-path documents (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 pedal lockups) has not been formally lifted.

native.verdict: Block-serial chaining (one block per Native instance, in series) equals one instance at -67 to -79 dB above 20 Hz on the tested chains (ledger 2026-10-15T19:21:10+00:00; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, T045 block-serial spike). Mono only; dual cabs and stereo untested (stereo is out of scope).

capabilities.capability: Use the whole block and model catalog

stomp.verdict: In principle any compatible model can be written with no capture, because the pedal runs it itself. Tried so far: the amps, cabs, drives and delays in the test presets, on firmware 3.50. Whether the 90 models gated by firmware now work on 3.80 has not been rechecked (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp firmware upgrade, human).

native.verdict: Only through a per-block library, which is not captured yet: about 661 models at {t:capture:native} each is the plan (T048), and one capture may carry up to 8 blocks (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass). Until then only the few chains captured so far can be rendered.

stomp.verdict: {t:render_2s:stomp} for a 2 s clip (the pedal plays the audio in real time); a 10 s clip is {t:render_10s:stomp}. Two-chain passes double throughput (see above).

native.verdict: {t:render_2s:native} for a 2 s clip and {t:render_10s:native} for a 10 s clip including 3 s of pre-roll. A pool of parallel hosts is faster again (timing tables below).

stomp.verdict: Snapshot values are written into the document and must equal the block values (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 snapshot values, lead on stomp-engine T051). Switching snapshots by MIDI (CC 69) recalls the stored values (ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00). Switching during a render is not tested.

native.verdict: Native renders the block values and ignores snapshot values when a file is loaded (ledger 2026-10-15T19:42:45+00:00). Snapshots are not switched in Native.

both.verdict: On the test presets the engines null against each other at -31 to -40 dB (K, A, B0, B00; ledger 2026-10-15T21:37:31+00:00), the pass line being -30 dB. Two known exceptions: cab Early Reflections match only at 0 (-31.4 dB at 0, -3.6 dB at 0.78; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 parity finding cab EarlyReflections), and delay echoes arrive about 1.48 ms later per echo on Native, so delay tails cannot null and are compared by level and timing (ledger 2026-10-15T21:14:14+00:00; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 Stomp T056 outcomes).

stomp.verdict: Open problem: any control session leaves the pedal's block editing locked until USB is unplugged, and the firmware 3.80 upgrade did not fix it (ledger 2026-10-15T22:36:17+00:00; T059). One earlier control wedge needed a power cycle (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 HX Stomp priorities, human).

native.verdict: Memory growth and crashes are fixed: the host stays at about 3.0 GB and repeats are identical to -313 dB (ledger 2026-10-15T18:54:10+00:00; DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, host memory). Captures need a logged-in screen session.

stomp.verdict: Tested on macOS only. Linux is expected to work and Windows is unconfirmed; both are set aside for now (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 HX Stomp priorities, human). The pedal is now on firmware 3.80, so everything measured on 3.50 awaits a recheck.

native.verdict: Tested on macOS with Native 3.82 as a VST3 plug-in in a helper process. Other platforms untested. Real MIDI control into the AU build did not change parameters (DECISIONS 2026-10-15 native-engine, Native phase 2 block bypass).
